commit_reviews.summary: Adds rate limiting, `/history` pagination, and TTL cleanup as well-integrated cross-cutting features that follow the module's env-config, section-banner, and task-lifecycle conventions.

compounding_issues: Seed app.py (Flask Todo) was abandoned wholesale in Session 1's greenfield rewrite and left as dead, unreferenced code in the repo for all 5 sessions — no integration, removal, or migration decision was ever made.

Session 4's transport abstraction relies on a module-level global `transport` reference set only inside main(); broadcast()/broadcast_to_channel() will raise AttributeError if invoked outside the serve context, an ordering coupling that later features silently depend on.

Session 3's SQLite/Redis integration uses `except Exception: pass` everywhere, and Session 5's rate limiting reuses the same pattern — failures degrade silently, making the multi-instance guarantees (Redis fan-out, persistence) best-effort rather than verified.

All logic accumulated in a single 613-line server.py with global singletons (registry, transport, rate-limit cache, Redis pool), forcing Session 5 to add more module-level state and tests to repeatedly reset globals in fixtures.
In-memory rate-limit fallback cache entries for disconnected clients are never evicted, so under sustained churn the dict grows without bound when Redis is absent.
key_decisions: Session 1: Rebuild the seed as an asyncio + websockets server in server.py, discarding the Flask app.py baseline entirely.
Session 2: Introduce a channel/subscription model with an in-memory registry keyed by websocket, routing broadcast vs channel-delivered messages.
Session 3: Add SQLite message persistence plus Redis pub/sub for multi-instance fan-out, with graceful in-memory/disk fallback when Redis is absent.
Session 4: Extract a BaseTransport ABC with WebSocketTransport + factory and centralize all sending behind a module-level transport reference, enabling future transport plug-ins.
Session 5: Implement dual-path rate limiting (Redis INCR/EXPIRE vs in-memory window), a /history endpoint with has_more cursor, and TTL-based message cleanup.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically. Test coverage grew 10 → 20 → 29 → 29 → 39 tests with every session ending green (no regressions). Session 1 delivered a clean single-file async server; Session 2 added a tidy channel feature; Session 3 layered on persistence and multi-instance fan-out while debugging fixture isolation; Session 4 was a genuine structural improvement that extracted a clean transport abstraction and verified the public API stayed intact; Session 5 closed the loop with cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, history, retention) plus 10 new tests. The only flat spot is that the refactor session added no new coverage, but it preserved all 29 existing tests.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, steadily improving 5-session arc that grew a bare WebSocket server into a feature-complete notification service with channels, persistence, Redis scale-out, transport abstraction, and cross-cutting hardening — slightly marred by abandoning the seed codebase and accumulating global state.
